test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: As per the the Industrial Policy Statement, 1977 a tiny unit was one which has an investment of Rs. ____ lakh.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Industrial Policy Statement of 1977** was announced by the **Janata Party government** on **December 23, 1977**.
 
• This policy was presented in the **Parliament** by the then Union Minister of Industry, **George Fernandes**.
 
• The policy introduced the concept of the **"Tiny Sector"** for the first time to promote rural industrialization and decentralization.
 
• As per the 1977 policy, a **tiny unit** was defined as an industrial unit with an investment in **machinery and equipment** of up to **Rs. 1 lakh**.
 
• To qualify as a tiny unit, the enterprise also had to be located in **villages or towns** with a population of less than **50,000** according to the **1971 Census**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Focus of 1977 Policy**: The primary objective was the **effective promotion of cottage and small-scale industries** widely dispersed in rural areas and small towns. It aimed to generate **large-scale employment** and reduce the concentration of economic power.
 
• **Classification of Small Sector**: The policy divided the small sector into three distinct categories:
 
 
• **Cottage and Household Industries**: Aimed at providing self-employment.
 
• **Tiny Sector**: Investment up to **Rs. 1 lakh** in rural/semi-urban areas.
 
• **Small Scale Industries (SSI)**: Investment limit up to **Rs. 10 lakhs**.
 
 
 
• **District Industries Centers (DIC)**: The 1977 policy proposed the establishment of **DICs** in every district. These centers were designed to provide all the services and support required by small and tiny entrepreneurs, such as **raw materials, credit, and marketing assistance**, under a single roof.
 
• **Reservation of Items**: To protect small-scale industries from competition with large-scale industries, the number of items reserved for exclusive production in the small sector was increased from **180 to 504**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ancillary Units**: Under the same 1977 policy, the investment limit for **ancillary units** (units supplying parts to large industries) was set at **Rs. 15 lakhs**.
 
• **Revival of Khadi**: The policy placed a heavy emphasis on the **Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)** to promote the use of handloom fabrics and traditional crafts.
 
• **Policy Evolution**: The investment limits for the tiny sector were later revised in subsequent policies. In the **Industrial Policy Statement of 1980**, the limit for tiny units was increased to **Rs. 2 lakhs**.
 
• **Demographic Criteria**: The **50,000 population** threshold was a critical feature of the 1977 policy to ensure that industrial benefits reached the **rural hinterland** rather than being clustered around metropolitan hubs.
